_comment: The recorded outcome of every gating test: the ones written BEFORE the code
they gate, which are therefore red on purpose. ci/expected-outcomes.py runs
each and fails when its outcome differs from the one recorded here IN EITHER
DIRECTION -- so a permanently red gate does not make every later change
unmergeable, and a gate that quietly turns green does not go unnoticed.
A RED ENTRY IS A DEBT. It names the task that closes it, and
ci/gates/expected_outcomes.py fails an entry that names none or names one
that does not exist. Advancing an outcome to green is only legitimate in the
same change that turns the test green; doing it alone fails the runner.
_key: <package directory, from the repository root>:<test function name>

conformance/e2e:TestRequestOctetsReachTh.why: The request-direction exact-bytes gate. Written at task 4.3, before the proxy exists, so the gap between the plan and a working chain is visible in CI from the first week rather than discovered at section 38. It fails today naming the absent proxy.

conformance/e2e:TestResponseOctetsReachT.why: The response-direction twin, written at task 4.4. Its closing task is the one that first delivers a response body to a client; design.md states that if either gate has not turned green by the end of section 38, the ordering has failed and the remaining sequence is re-planned.
